newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt denies plane took military goods to Burundi.
newsitem.headline: Egypt denies plane took military goods to Burundi.

text.p: Egypt denied on Monday that an Egyptian plane took military equipment last week to Burundi, where ethnic strife has claimed tens of thousands of lives.
A foreign ministry statement also said Egypt had not made any deals with Burundi for a long period because of its desire to see a peaceful settlement in the Great Lakes region.
A Burundian rebel group said on Saturday an Egyptian plane unloaded munitions and military uniforms at the capital Bujumbura on Friday in violation of regional sanctions.
The National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) made the accusation in a letter to the Tanzanian chairman of a regional committee monitoring the sanctions.
It said the plane's manifest, registered at Bujumbura airport, listed it as flying from Ostend in Belgium to Lubumbashi, Zaire, with 34 tonnes of cargo described as "Consolidation".
The Egyptian statement said: "A spokesman for the Foreign Ministry denied news agency reports about the arrival of an Egyptian plane in Burundi carrying military material.
"He said that Egypt has not made any deals with Burundi for a long period, in the context of its desire to settle the situation in the Great Lakes region by peaceful means."
It said an Egyptian assistant foreign minister would visit the region soon to deliver relief supplies.
